summary: This is a Mol Labs public research report (card N8) proposing a pre-registered hypothesis that Azure B, a methylene blue (MB) metabolite with ~6× stronger MAO-A potency, fails to match MB's memory rescue on a cytochrome oxidase (COX)-inhibitor amnestic retention assay. The experiment has NOT been run; the claim is a prediction grounded in existing literature on MB's COX-amnestic rescue and Azure B's MAO-A enzyme potency. The document explicitly flags that prior cards N5–N7 do not prove this failure and that the Azure B vs. MB COX-amnestic head-to-head remains UNKNOWN.

content_blocks.title: Core Claim / Hypothesis
content_blocks.content: On a pre-registered cytochrome-oxidase (COX)-inhibitor amnestic retention assay where parent methylene blue (MB) restores memory, Azure B fails to match that rescue — retention Δ ≤70% of MB (or outside a pre-registered MB-equivalence band) — despite Azure B's stronger MAO-A potency under matched enzyme conditions. This is a PREDICTION; the experiment has NOT been run.

content_blocks.title: Scientific Rationale / Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: The hypothesis is framed as a 'redox-vs-MAO assumption-kill' on the COX-amnestic / metabolic-memory class. If MB's memory rescue tracks MAO-A potency, Azure B (~6× stronger MAO-A than MB per Petzer 2012) should match or exceed parent MB. If rescue tracks parent redox / COX-facing structure, Azure B underperforms on the same retention panel. Key literature anchors: (1) Callaway 2002 / Gonzalez-Lima class — low-dose MB restores spatial retention after COX inhibition (PMID 12384216). (2) Rojas 2011 — MB shows beneficial network effects in an amnestic model (PMID 21087672). (3) Petzer 2012 — Azure B high-potency reversible MAO-A ~6× MB (PMID 22197611). (4) Ramsay 2007 — MB potent reversible MAO-A inhibitor (PMID 17721552).

content_blocks.title: Prior Art / Literature Evidence
content_blocks.content:
Four key references cited:
1. PMID 12384216 / DOI 10.1016/s0304-3940(02)00827-3 — Low-dose MB restores spatial memory retention impaired by a cytochrome oxidase inhibitor (Callaway / Gonzalez-Lima class). No Azure B arm.
2. PMID 21087672 / DOI 10.1016/j.neuroimage.2010.11.023 / PMC3026638 — MB beneficial network effects in an amnestic model (metabolic/network framing). No Azure B arm.
3. PMID 22197611 / DOI 10.1016/j.taap.2011.12.005 — Azure B high-potency reversible MAO-A (~6× MB under matched conditions) (Petzer 2012). Enzyme data only, not COX-amnestic cognition.
4. PMID 17721552 / DOI 10.1038/sj.bjp.0707430 / PMC2078225 — MB potent reversible MAO-A inhibitor; serotonin-toxicity prediction (Ramsay 2007).

content_blocks.title: Baseline Measured / Evidence State
content_blocks.content: MB COX-amnestic / amnestic-network rescue: LITERATURE (PMID 12384216; 21087672). Azure B stronger MAO-A than MB: LITERATURE (PMID 22197611). MB MAO-A potency: LITERATURE (PMID 17721552). Azure B vs parent MB on the same COX-amnestic rescue / retention panel: UNKNOWN (soft-complete Azure B∩MB∩memory/rescue = 0; Azure B∩COX/amnestic hits = false positives only). ≤70% MB-equivalence fail: PREDICTION. N5–N7 do not already prove this failure — generic WM / redox-dead / selective MAO-A-i arms only; soft-complete empty ≠ failure.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. Do not treat N5–N7 as proving N8 — N6 asked Azure B ≠ MB on generic WM (soft-complete); N7 redox-dead×WM; N5 selective MAO-A-i; none measured Azure B on the Gonzalez-Lima COX-amnestic rescue.
2. MAO IC50 ≠ brain rescue PD — Petzer/Ramsay are enzyme inhibition; no COX-amnestic cognition endpoint for Azure B.
3. PK / brain exposure + assay identity — Azure B could underperform from distribution; lock the same COX-inhibitor amnestic / spatial or discrimination retention class where parent MB restores — not a new generic WM substitute. Soft-complete empty ≠ negative result. No dosing.

content_blocks.title: Ablation Analysis
content_blocks.content:
Three critical ablations identified:
1. Remove same COX-amnestic/retention contrast of Azure B vs parent MB: Without the behavioral head-to-head on the Gonzalez-Lima class assay, MB rescue LITERATURE and Azure B MAO LITERATURE cannot show Azure B fails to match MB rescue.
2. Remove stronger-MAO-A / MAO-comparable framing (Azure B vs MB enzyme potency anchor): Without the potency contrast, underperformance is just 'Azure B weak,' not an assumption-kill of MAOI-explains-COX-amnestic-rescue.
3. Remove N5–N7≠proof + soft-complete-empty≠failure + assay-identity discipline: Treating N5–N7 or empty/false-positive PubMed as already deciding Azure B COX-amnestic failure would invent a negative result left UNKNOWN.

content_blocks.title: Refutation Criteria and Human Guidance
content_blocks.content:
Refute if: On the pre-registered COX-inhibitor amnestic retention assay, Azure B matches parent MB within the MB-equivalence band (retention Δ >70% of MB or inside band) — especially under exposure/occupancy-matched conditions — so MAO-potency / metabolite-sufficiency for metabolic-memory rescue survives.

Ask a human: Lock COX-inhibitor amnestic assay identity (spatial vs discrimination retention class where parent MB restores), Azure B vs MB exposure/occupancy readout, and optional selective MAO-A-i arm before treating any MB metabolic-memory rescue as metabolite-MAO; do not treat N5–N7 as already proving Azure B COX-amnestic failure; no dosing.

key_findings: Experiment NOT RUN — N8 is a proposed assay / prediction, not an executed study. Execution status: NOT_RUN.
Core prediction: Azure B will fail to match methylene blue (MB) on a COX-inhibitor amnestic retention assay (threshold: retention Δ ≤70% of MB or outside pre-registered MB-equivalence band).
Azure B has ~6× stronger reversible MAO-A potency than MB under matched enzyme conditions (Petzer 2012, PMID 22197611) — enzyme data only, no in vivo cognition endpoint.
MB restores spatial memory retention after COX inhibition in the Callaway/Gonzalez-Lima class assay (PMID 12384216) — no Azure B arm exists in the literature.
MB shows beneficial network effects in an amnestic model (PMID 21087672) — no Azure B arm.
Azure B vs MB on the same COX-amnestic rescue panel is UNKNOWN: soft-complete search returned 0 hits / false positives only.
Prior cards N5–N7 do NOT prove Azure B COX-amnestic rescue failure — they tested generic WM, redox-dead arms, and selective MAO-A-i, not the Gonzalez-Lima COX-amnestic rescue.
Competing falsifier path: if Azure B matches MB once brain exposure/MAO occupancy is matched, PK distribution (not redox structure) explains any underperformance.
Kill cost tier 1; estimated time to refute: 4 weeks. IP class: redox-vs-MAO. FTO status: UNKNOWN.
TRL assessment: TRL 1 — concept/hypothesis only; no experimental data generated for this specific claim.
